summary: A research-tools server reached over MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST) or a plain JSON API. A council app calls it from its Ask Council chat only, never from grades, rating runs or scheduled council runs, and shows each quoted number with its cite url and data_through date, keeping the label.
instructions: Research tools of a small fund's console. Prices are daily closes and never later than today; FX rates are units per US dollar. Backtests decide on one close and trade at the next, after costs. Paper portfolios are simulated and never reach a broker. Every call is logged, and names on the firm's restricted list are refused or flagged. Each result has a cite block: quote its url and data_through beside any number you use, and keep its label.

call_tool.body: the tool's arguments as a JSON object

headers.Authorization: Bearer <key>; one key per app, made by an admin, revocable
headers.X-Correlation-Id: optional, 8 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ; send the id of the person's question so the app's audit entry and the server's tool-call entries can be joined
headers.X-Model-Location: local or cloud: where the model that will read the result runs. Recorded on every call. When compliance limits council research to local models, calls without 'local' are refused

council_key.may: every look-up, and run backtests, forecasts and nowcasts
council_key.limits: per key: 60 calls a minute, 30 runs an hour, and a daily run cap set by the firm (100 until set). The app should also cap tool calls per question (4 suggested)
council_key.book_data: none: no tool reads positions, NAV or the book. VaR, sizing and Monte Carlo stay inside the server

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: Instruments with research price history, and the days each one covers.

tools.name: get_prices
tools.description: Daily closes for one instrument, never past today. Default: the last year. Adjusted for splits and dividends unless adjusted is false.

tools.name: run_backtest
tools.description: Run a strategy backtest and save it. A spec is an object: name (text; runs with one name are one family for the deflated Sharpe), universe (list of symbols set up in the console), start and end (YYYY-MM-DD), signal {kind: buy_and_hold | momentum (lookback, skip) | trend (fast, slow) | mean_reversion (lookback) | low_vol (lookback) | carry (FX only: RATE.<currency> less RATE.USD) | macro (series {symbol: CODE}, direction 1 or -1, change in days)}, and optionally select {top, long_short}, sizing {kind: equal | inverse_vol | signal, lookback}, rebalance (never | daily | weekly | monthly | quarterly), limits {max_weight, gross} as fractions, vol_target, costs_bp, benchmark (a symbol), train_fraction, and walk_forward {param, values, train_days, test_days}. Signals see only data known at each decision day's close; trades fill at the next close, after costs.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: One saved backtest: spec, measures, equity curve and flags.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: The most recent backtests, newest first.

tools.name: compare_runs
tools.description: Measures of 2 to 6 backtests side by side.

tools.name: list_macro_series
tools.description: Macro and factor series on file, with the periods covered.

tools.name: get_macro_series
tools.description: One macro series' values as known at the close of as_of (default today), so later revisions don't leak into the past.

tools.name: describe_series
tools.description: Summary statistics of one return series: mean, volatility, Sharpe, skew, kurtosis, autocorrelation, drawdown, VaR and expected shortfall. ref is a symbol, a backtest id (BTR-...), a paper id (PPF-...) or macro:CODE.

tools.name: correlations
tools.description: Correlation matrix of 2 to 12 return series on the days they share. Each ref is a symbol, a backtest id (BTR-...), a paper id (PPF-...) or macro:CODE.

tools.name: regress
tools.description: Regress one return series on 1 to 8 factor series (OLS with alpha): betas, t-statistics, R squared. Each is a symbol, a backtest id (BTR-...), a paper id (PPF-...) or macro:CODE.

tools.name: forecast_series
tools.description: Forecast a series and save the forecast. model arima: the level of a symbol's closes (FX as quoted) or of macro:CODE, order chosen by AIC, with 80% and 95% bands and a check against a naive forecast on held-out data. model garch: the volatility of returns (symbol, BTR-..., PPF-... or macro:CODE), daily and annualised. Reads only what was known at the close of as_of (default today).

tools.name: get_forecast
tools.description: One saved forecast by forecast_id, or the most recent ones without it.

tools.name: list_nowcasts
tools.description: Nowcast models (a quarterly target such as a country's GDP growth, monthly indicators) with each one's latest nowcast.

tools.name: get_nowcast
tools.description: A nowcast model's latest estimate for the quarter with its 80% band, the backcast of last quarter if not yet published, what moved it since the run before (each release's surprise times its weight, revisions, re-estimation), and the history of nowcasts.

tools.name: run_nowcast
tools.description: Run a nowcast model on the macro data known at the close of as_of (default today) and save it. A day already run on the same data returns that run.

tools.name: option_price
tools.description: Price and Greeks of one equity option (right call or put, style american or european). vol is a yearly fraction (0.25) and defaults to GARCH's forecast to expiry; with price, also the implied volatility and whether it is rich or cheap against GARCH. Needs the Options module.

tools.name: option_chain
tools.description: The latest stored option chain for a symbol: each expiry's at-the-money implied volatility against GARCH (rich, fair or cheap) and one expiry's smile near the money (default: the first at least three weeks out). Needs the Options module.

tools.name: paper_status
tools.description: One paper portfolio with its last 60 days, or all of them without portfolio_id.

cite.where: every successful result has a top-level 'cite' object

fields.id: the saved run's id, or null for a plain look-up
fields.url: link to the run's page on the server, or null
fields.data_through: YYYY-MM-DD: the last day of data the result uses, or null
fields.label: Hypothetical, past performance; not a recommendation

rules: Quote numbers only from the result; an app's number or citation check should treat the result as the source.
Show the label and the url beside the figures.
Never turn a result into a buy or sell call.

restricted_names: The server applies the firm's restricted-list rule: calls on restricted or watch-list names are logged and shown to compliance, or refused if compliance set research to block. 'flagged' lists flagged instrument ids; the app should not print them

429.error: Too many calls; try again in N seconds

refusals.app_behaviour: On any refusal or no answer within the app's timeout, say 'Research tools unavailable' with the reason and answer the rest of the question without them

cite.label: Hypothetical, past performance; not a recommendation

examples.what: A council key asking for a paper portfolio

content.text: Council keys can't start paper portfolios; a person starts one on Research > Paper
